title: Otto powerbank 10K mAh $10 @ Officeworks (was $30)
body:
Deal: Otto powerbank 10K mAh $10 @ Officeworks (was $30)

[dangerdanger] Stock checker
Other designs were $9 some time back , they need to clear them out at much lower price
[Big L] Thanks for that, saved me mucking about looking. None of the leaf print type in Vic.
Lilac: https://officeworks.youinstock.com.au/search/OTPBPL18W/vic
Rainbow: https://officeworks.youinstock.com.au/search/OTPBRW18W/vic
Pink: https://officeworks.youinstock.com.au/search/OTPBPK18W/vic
Elsternwick is the best spot and has all but Leaf print.
[WwDesi] Looks like no stock in SA tried all close store to me none
[Lord Ra] Does this support fast charging? Or super fast charging?
[A 1] See comment above (18w) or click the link (18w).
It's 18w output, greater than the 5w baseline from years past. Modern phones now often accept 20-45w charging, or more. Higher wattage = faster charge rate.
[SiliconeFries] At 18W, this 10k mAH powerbank is considered slow charging. It will take about 3.5 hours to charge itself to full and about 2.5 hours to charge an iPhone 17 Pro Max. It's borderline e-waste. Buy something with at least 65W charging.
[T_double_U] Hmmm I ordered 2 and you’re making me want to cancel.
[SiliconeFries] Cancel or give them away as Christmas presents to someone you don't like
[T_double_U] @SiliconeFries: Haha I like that idea. However upon doing more research, my iPhone 11 Pro Max has a maximum charge rate of 22W so I’m only missing out on a few watts so I think this might still work for me.
[SiliconeFries] @T_double_U: And they're good to power USB fairy lights in the car or camping
[bio] Where can I find "something with at least 65W" for $10?
Also how many phones support 65W charging? Your iPhone 17 Pro Max can only do 40W.
[SiliconeFries] You won't find a 65W powerbank for $10. But that's not a good reason to buy this junk. Invest a little in a powerbank with 65W input/output and pass-through charging, it'll actually be useful. $50 for a 65W 20,000 mAh powerbank on Amazon.
[Lord Ra] Thanks mate. Your answer is what I was looking for. The 18w meant nothing for me. I know higher is better, but I have no idea of scale. I won't get any.
[Borg] Depends on your use case. These are handy for: example only: a tablet sitting on a table away from mains power. Keeps it topped up throughout the day to save tablets battery draining down.
Many other things as long as not looking for high watt output (although 18w isn’t bad) or large capacity being only 10000mAh.
[SiliconeFries] True, but it's use cases are limited. The main downsides of this powerbank, and there are many, are that it doesn't support pass-through charging and it takes 3.5 hours to charge itself. It's a paperweight for those 3.5 hours.
[Big L] @SiliconeFries: Power-banks are a paperweight more often than they're not. You're talking bollocks, and assuming everyone's use case is similar to yours.
[SiliconeFries] @Big L: You really should treat yourself to one of these powebanks, you deserve it.
[Big L] @SiliconeFries: I'd have bought one for $10, and it'd be fine for the rare occasion I'd need it.
Tell everyone what power-bank you own with at least 65W pass-through charging for your iPhone 17 Pro Max.
[SiliconeFries] @Big L: You seem angry and confrontational. Is everything OK? Would you like to talk about it?
[tanabe88gg] @SiliconeFries: Come on mate, I know sometimes it is hard to appreciate that someone else might have different values to your own. Try to think of the glass being half full for once! I bet if you put your mind to it you could think of at least 3 cases where this would be ideal, even without being snide about it.
[Big L] @SiliconeFries: Are the other people who called you out angry and confrontational too?
You still haven't made a recommendation.
[carrawa] Could be used for USB lighting, especially in a power outage.
[Borg] Exactly. There are many many good use cases. I have a outdoor gazebo that has lights. I use powerbank instead of D Batteries. 10000mAh lasts 24 hours or longer. I recharge every few days so have never reached 0% to know exact hrs..
